{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693543449,"sessionID":"ses_e23f023d6ffehOUDHDUlEAjR57","part":{"id":"prt_1dc1235b1001fSBcAjCTFOOsYT","messageID":"msg_1dc121507001hqOZ7pdeypg228","sessionID":"ses_e23f023d6ffehOUDHDUlEAjR57","type":"text","text":"The shift is over. All four customer-facing services have been at 0% errors since minute 73, and they stayed there through minute 120 with nothing new breaking.\n\nI found four causes and fixed each one:\n\n1. **payments-db** (behind most of the mobile-api failures and part of web-storefront's): a config change at minute −23 cut its database connection pool from 40 to 4. I reverted it. Its callers' retries kept it overloaded afterwards, so I throttled it to 60% from minute 18 to 25 to end that, then lifted the throttle.\n2. **import-svc** (behind partner-api's errors, the expensive service): a deploy at minute −19 switched its data format to \"v3\", which notifications-svc couldn't read. I rolled it back at minute 40. While the rollback ran, partner-api's errors briefly rose to about 55%, and the rollback's own failures set off a retry storm on import-svc. A 60% throttle from minute 46 to 51 cleared it, and partner-api has been at 0% since.\n3. **recommendations-svc** (the rest of mobile-api's errors): it didn't have enough capacity and was rejecting about 42% of requests. I scaled it from 4 to 8 replicas, which landed at minute 46. That costs $12/min until the end of the shift.\n4. **identity-svc** (a new fault at minute 45 that took web-storefront and mobile-api to about 94% errors through catalog-svc): a deploy (v153) started reading the currency field without a default value. I rolled it back. A 70% throttle from minute 68 to 72 cleared the retry storm, and everything has been at 0% since minute 73.\n\nI left two things alone on purpose:\n- **push-svc** had a high-CPU alert the whole shift but almost no errors, so I didn't touch it.\n- **recommendations-svc** stays at 8 replicas: it still runs at about 88% CPU on 8, so going lower would overload it again. I didn't look for why its capacity per replica dropped. A rollback there would have failed about 30% of mobile-api requests for 6 minutes, which costs more than the extra replicas.\n\nNo throttles are still on.","time":{"start":1794693543345,"end":1794693543440}}}
